attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own June 2022 passage and explicitly re-endorses it in 2025, saying it still applies to today's LLMs and to Claude. These are his words and he endorses them.

semantics.note: The normalisation captures the core assertion: no connection to the world, just autocomplete. It drops the 'doesn't even try' design element, but the contract restores it. The claim is a present-tense observation with no hedging.

contract.note: Marcus supplied no test. The plain reading treats the claim as being about semantic grounding, not retrieval or the training objective. That is the ordinary reading in context and is not stretched either way. The result still turns on a contested line between linguistic association and reference.

evidence.note: Google's primary paper confirms the next-token pretraining objective. An objective does not show what representations the model learns, and the paper's source-attribution 'groundedness' is a different sense of the word.

This peer-reviewed position paper argues that a system trained only on form cannot learn meaning. It is a philosophical argument that predates the named systems, so under the source rules it cannot establish their actual capabilities.

Anthropic reports interventions on Claude's intermediate concept features that change its answers. This challenges a pure word-association account, but it is a company disclosure about its own model, covers a limited method, and does not show grounding to real-world referents.

reviews.rationale: No item meets the support or contradiction condition. e1 shows only the training objective. e2 is a philosophical argument made before these systems existed. e3 is a company disclosure: it points against a simple autocomplete account but does not establish semantic grounding independently. The packet itself says there is no decisive test separating semantic reference from linguistic association, so the outcome is unresolved.
